title: Every integer has an additive inverse

formal.statement: theorem Int.add_neg : ((x0 : Int) -> Eq.{1} Int (Int.add x0 (Int.neg x0)) Int.zero)

evidence.notes: `build_int_prelude` admits this theorem through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so a green run of the command is a machine-checked proof. Measured 2026-08-14: 12 tests pass (a nonzero count -- the filter is not inert).

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- this theorem's trusted closure is empty
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example int_theorem_inventory -- add_neg 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^theorem[[:space:]]+Int\.add_neg[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Two independent bounds, because either alone would be weaker than it looks. (1) `Kernel::axiom_footprint` walks THIS declaration's transitive dependencies and prints an empty footprint column -- this is the kernel's `#print axioms`, and it is the check that matters, since an integer law IS still asserted (`Int.euclidean_decomposition`; it was 6 until lane int-remainder proved the `subNatNat` borrow, and the check mattered more then) and Int.add_neg could have reached for one and still type-checked. (2) `nat_axiom_inventory` reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0` for the development ZZ is constructed over, so the foundation admits no trusted declaration at all. Counting `Declaration::Axiom` alone would not have sufficed: `Opaque` has no proof body and `Quotient` admits `Quot.sound`, which is exactly the declaration the quotient-of-NxN construction would have added -- the enumeration covers all three kinds and reports zero for each.

evidence.supports: `Int.add` and `Int.neg` are the intended operations, not merely operations satisfying this law
evidence.notes: A wrong `Int.add` would satisfy a wrong-but-provable `add_neg`, so the theorem alone does not pin the operation down. This test evaluates 16 additions and multiplications and 5 negations by kernel reduction against their normal forms, covering every sign combination including the borrow cases where `Int.subNatNat` has to decide which constructor the answer lands in (3 + (-3) = 0 and 1 + (-3) = -2 are both present).

provenance.source: one of the 34 propositions build_int_prelude previously ASSERTED; this lane constructed ZZ over the proved Nat development and derived it

notes: This is the law that makes ZZ a group and the one that fails for the naive representation. On the raw pair (a,b) meaning a-b, commutativity and associativity of addition hold structurally, but (a,b)+(b,a) = (a+b, b+a), which is not the pair (0,0) -- so an additive inverse exists only after quotienting. Taking that quotient in this kernel would admit `Quot`/`Quot.sound` as `Declaration::Quotient`, putting `Quot.sound` in this fact's footprint permanently. The normalized `Int.ofNat`/`Int.negSucc` representation avoids it, which is why `axiom_footprint: []` is available here at all. The proof rests on `Nat.sub_self` (not itself in this ledger): `Int.subNatNat n n` puts `Nat.sub n n` in both its scrutinee and its non-negative value, so one rewrite collapses both. formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `int_theorem_inventory`; it was not transcribed by hand.
